1: # macOS Native Server M005 — Forwarding, PF/NAT Policy, and Gateway Feasibility Decision
     2: 
     3: Disposition: **blocked** (narrowed 2026-10-14: effective NAT traffic still
     4: unqualified — platform attachment refused + no v6 uplink; everything else
     5: qualified live on both arches).
     6: 
     7: Date: 2026-10-13 (policy decision + blocked record); 2026-10-14 (hosted evidence).
     8: 
     9: ## Implementation revision
    10: 
    11: - Repository baseline: `ee605aa` (M004 blocked closure).
    12: - Qualified implementation head: `be077d1944588bdc82a285434098d2d2fdf75a11`.
    13: - Source plan: `plans/implementation/macos-native-server/005-forwarding-pf-nat-and-platform-policy.md` (policy-ready → blocked by this record).
    14: 
    15: ## The M005 distribution decision (explicit gate review)
    16: 
    17: Apple TN3165 (`Packet Filter Is Not API`) warns PF is not a product API for
    18: broadly distributed software; it is intended for system implementations and
    19: advanced user/admin use. Reviewed against the wg-basic appliance model:
    20: 
    21: - **Decision: advanced-administrator opt-in ONLY. General consumer macOS
    22:   gateway support is NOT claimed and MUST NOT be advertised.**
    23: - The administrator explicitly attaches the installation anchor from their
    24:   own PF configuration. wg-basic never rewrites `/etc/pf.conf`, flushes any
    25:   table, disables or enables PF globally, or seizes global forwarding.
    26: - Without a verified parent attachment, the backend reports degraded and
    27:   applies nothing (fail closed with an actionable error).
    28: - IPv4: forwarding + masquerade through the dedicated anchor, opt-in only.
    29:   IPv6: routed return, categorically never NAT66.
    30: - Global forwarding toggles are shared and sticky: observed read-only,
    31:   enabled only when the explicit policy requires, never silently reset on
    32:   disable/teardown.
    33: - If a future Apple-supported server-grade NAT integration appears, this
    34:   decision returns to ADR-008 review rather than stretching PF further.
    35: 
    36: This decision gates M006 (the installer MUST NOT auto-modify PF configuration;
    37: launchd + helper provenance proceed independently) and M007 (release claims
    38: must label macOS gateway as advanced-admin-only).
    39: 
    40: ## Requirement-to-evidence matrix
    41: 
    42: | Requirement (plan) | Evidence | Result |
    43: |---|---|---|
    44: | §5.1 Research + addendum/ADR gate: advanced-admin mode, explicit setup, distribution compatibility; alternate strategy or re-scope if unacceptable | This record is the gate: TN3165 reviewed, advanced-admin-only mode defined with explicit-setup + no-auto-mutation rules above; no alternate architecture needed because the narrowed scope is lawful for expert-operated headless installs. Re-scope applied (no general gateway claim) rather than disguised risk | Passed (decision recorded) |
    45: | §5.2 Read-only PF inventory + anchor attachment verification (nat + filter order); conflicts with existing PF, managers, Internet Sharing, SIP | Attempted unprivileged on native host: `pfctl -s info` → `/dev/pf: Permission denied` (PF is root-gated even for reads — inventory itself needs privilege, recorded honestly); `sysctl net.inet.ip.forwarding/net.inet6.ip6.forwarding` → `0`/`0` read-only (observed, never mutated). Attachment verification modeled purely (`attachment_verified` requires parent invocation, not mere existence) with fixture tests | Passed (read-only facts; live inventory blocked on root) |
    46: | §5.3 Bounded dedicated anchor + predictable rules + admin instructions; no implicit parent mutation; owner marker/digest/drift fail-closed; bounded internally rendered pfctl only, never shell/user text | `src/firewall/pf.rs`: `anchor_name` (installation-scoped deterministic), `render_policy` (IPv4 masquerade, NAT66 excluded by `is_ipv4` gate), `rules_digest` drift detection, `teardown_order`. No `Command`/shell/`pfctl -f`/`/etc/pf.conf` in the module (guard-pinned); bounded invocation designed but deliberately not implemented until live qualification | Passed (model; execution blocked) |
    47: | §5.4 Controlled forwarding sysctl observe/enable; explicit policy, strict paths, no family toggles; persistence/reboot/operator steps; foreign preservation | Strict constants `net.inet.ip.forwarding` / `net.inet6.ip6.forwarding`; no caller sysctls expressible; observed values `0`/`0` left untouched; policy states enable-only-with-opt-in + never-reset (documented + modeled) | Passed (model; live enable blocked) |
    48: | §5.5 Observe/plan/apply/verify + teardown ordering; v4 no-NAT vs masquerade, v6 routed no-NAT66, firewall interactions; degraded reasons, no false convergence | Ordering modeled (`teardown_order`: filter-anchor → nat-anchor → helper; global/foreign never touched); `FirewallService` Darwin still returns `Unsupported` (no false convergence). Live demo needs root + helper | Partially passed (model), blocked (live) |
    49: | §5.6 Supported/unsupported configs + exact opt-in contract before M006 | Contract in the decision above + module docs; M006 installer constraint recorded (no PF auto-configuration) | Passed |
    50: | Native + regression tests (isolated admin-PF host: forwarded v4/NAT, routed v6, foreign preservation, drift/conflict/disabled/wrong-owner/Sharing cases; pfctl failure injection; Linux nft + dual-stack E2E regression) | Unit layer green (6 `firewall::pf` + purity guard); Linux suites untouched and green. Live traffic, anchor attach/drift, and failure injection need root on a disposable host | Partially passed (unit), **blocked** (live) |
    51: | Stop: silent unrelated-config rewrite, unacceptable distribution posture, unpreservable foreign state, failed NAT verification, seized global PF | Honored: no config write exists in the tree; posture resolved by narrowing (advanced-admin-only); foreign preservation modeled; no NAT claim made without traffic proof | Passed (by refusal to over-claim) |

    53: ## Verification
    54: 
    55: Local commands on native Darwin arm64 (macOS 26.6.2, rustc 1.89.0):
    56: 
    57: - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check/clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` (plus both Darwin triples), `cargo test --locked` (lib 372 incl. 6 new `firewall::pf`; 56/55+1 guards; integration green modulo the known transient parallel port race), `cargo +1.89.0 check` — passed.
    58: - Read-only host facts (zero mutation): `pfctl -s info` → permission denied (root-gated); `sysctl` forwarding `0`/`0` (observed only).
    59: - No `utun`, route, PF, sysctl, or forwarding mutation was performed in this session.
    60: 
    61: Privileged evidence NOT collected (blocker shared with M003/M004): effective forwarded IPv4 (no-NAT/NAT), routed IPv6 both directions, anchor attach + packet matching (not rule text), foreign-PF/Internet-Sharing coexistence, drift/conflict/PF-disabled/wrong-owner cases, `pfctl` timeout/failure injection, Linux nft + dual-stack E2E rerun at this head.
    62: 
    63: ## Security and ownership evidence
    64: 
    65: - No new privileged operation: `pf.rs` contains no process/shell/sysctl-write/file-write (guard `the_darwin_pf_model_renders_without_executing` green); `PROCESS_MODULES` unchanged (`[nft.rs, wireguard/darwin.rs]`).
    66: - Typed policy only (`DesiredNetworkPolicy` in, rendered anchor rules out); no remote raw PF anywhere; Linux `nft` owner-table claims never copied (anchors require parent invocation by design).
    67: - Linux firewall path untouched; Darwin live firewall still `Unsupported` (fail closed, degraded receipts truthful).
    68: 
    69: ## Documentation, limitations, and findings
    70: 
    71: - No current-behavior docs changed (no shipped gateway behavior). The decision + contract live here and in `src/firewall/pf.rs` docs; operator-facing PF prerequisites will be written when live qualification exists. `README` still claims Linux-native only.
    72: - Hard blocker (shared): disposable privileged Mac host + non-interactive root + explicit host-mutation opt-in for live gateway traffic. No packet claim made.
    73: - Downstream effect: M006 MUST NOT auto-configure PF (installer constraint recorded); M007 must label any macOS gateway claim advanced-admin-only with this decision cited.
    74: - Findings: no high/medium/low open items in the policy/model scope.
    75: 
    76: M005 is **blocked** on live gateway qualification with the decision above binding. M006 launchd/installation scope may proceed under the no-PF-mutation constraint; its native install evidence carries the same privileged-host blocker.

    78: ## Hosted live evidence 2026-10-14 (run `38524007872`, head `a10b4c2`)
    79: 
    80: Fixtures `live_pf_inventory_and_anchor_cycle` (5/5 arm64) and
    81: `live_forwarding_and_unattached_anchor_probe` (both arches), `macos-15`
    82: arm64 + `macos-15-intel` x86_64 native, macOS 15.7.9:
    83: 
    84: - Privileged PF inventory with root: `Status: Disabled`; forwarding
    85:   sysctls observed `0`/`0`, then cycled `0→1→0` with restore verified.
    86: - Rendered filter + NAT files parse under `pfctl -n`; filter rules stage
    87:   into the dedicated anchor and list back; NAT-only file stages too (an
    88:   earlier mixed filter+nat file tripped the guard — files stay split).
    89: - The main-ruleset replacement that would attach the anchor is refused by

    94: - With PF enabled and the anchor loaded, parent filter/NAT output still
    95:   shows no reference: attachment absent, policy inert by construction.
    96:   Diverted tunnel traffic (`8.8.8.8/32` via our `utun`, control-probed
    97:   direct first) provably fails without attachment — no false convergence.
    98: - Host restored in order: route deleted, anchor flushed, PF disabled
    99:   (verified), forwarding `0` (verified), helpers down, inventory baseline.
   100: - Evidence artifacts: `m005-pf-anchor-cycle.txt`,
   101:   `m005-platform-probe.txt` both arches on run `38524007872`.
   102: 
   103: What this means for the TN3165 decision: attachment requires replacing the
   104: system PF ruleset — exactly the host-level surgery the advanced-admin-only
   105: decision reserves to an explicit administrator. The decision stands,
   106: now evidence-backed. The remaining live tail is effective forwarded/NAT
   107: traffic (needs that attachment on a host where an admin performs it) plus
   108: IPv6 egress routing (no v6 uplink on hosted runners).
